# Debug

The text a value has for whoever is inspecting a program.

```rux
pub interface Debug {
    func WriteDebug(
        writer: &var TextWriter,
        spec: FormatSpec
    ) -> ! FormatError;
}
```

Debug output is diagnostic, not a serialization format: it may quote, escape, name fields, and show an invalid
value by its numeric form where [`Display`](/docs/api/text/display) would replace it. Nothing promises it can be parsed back.

## Requirements

<h3 id="write-debug"><code>WriteDebug</code></h3>

```rux
func WriteDebug(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes this value's inspection text under `spec`.
The same failures `WriteDisplay` may report, for the same reasons.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the value's complete text was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Display.rux#L46)

<h3 id="write-escaped"><code>WriteEscaped</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteEscaped(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    text: char8[..]
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes `text` with the characters that would be ambiguous or invisible replaced by escapes.
The quote and the backslash are escaped because they collide with the quoting around a debug rendering. The C0
and C1 control ranges are escaped because they act on a terminal rather than being read, and a value containing
one should say so rather than doing it. `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and `\0` get their short forms; every other control
becomes `\u{XX}`. Everything else, including all ordinary non-ASCII text, is written unchanged.
Runs of ordinary bytes are written in one call rather than byte by byte, so escaping costs a pass and not a
write per character.
Reports whatever the writer reported, stopping at the first refusal.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Presentation.rux#L87)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                        |
| -------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                    |
| `text`   | `char8[..]`       | the UTF-8 text to escape and write |

**Returns**: success when the escaped text was accepted

<h3 id="write-optional-debug"><code>WriteOptionalDebug&lt;T&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteOptionalDebug<T: Debug>(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    value: &T?,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes a borrowed optional as `Some(value)` or `none`.
The optional is borrowed and its payload with it, so this can be called on an optional holding a value that
cannot be copied, as many times as wanted, and the optional still holds it afterwards.
`spec` is handed to the payload's own `WriteDebug` and describes it rather than the wrapper.
Reports whatever the writer or the payload's implementation reported, stopping at the first refusal, so a
destination that has already refused something is not written to again.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Structure.rux#L34)

**Type parameters**

| Name       | Description                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `T: Debug` | the payload type, which must know how to show itself |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                                 |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                             |
| `value`  | `&T?`             | the optional to show, borrowed for the call |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what to show the payload under              |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted

<h3 id="write-fallible-debug"><code>WriteFallibleDebug&lt;T, E&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteFallibleDebug<T: Debug, E: Debug>(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    value: &(T ! E),
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes a borrowed fallible as `Success(value)` or `Failure(reason)`.
Both payloads are borrowed, so neither channel is consumed by being shown. The names are the native channel
names, so what is written names the case a reader would branch on.
`spec` is handed to whichever payload is present and describes it rather than the wrapper.
Reports whatever the writer or the payload's implementation reported, stopping at the first refusal.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Structure.rux#L60)

**Type parameters**

| Name       | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `T: Debug` | the success payload type, which must know how to show itself |
| `E: Debug` | the failure payload type, which must know how to show itself |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                                 |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                             |
| `value`  | `&(T ! E)`        | the fallible to show, borrowed for the call |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what to show the payload under              |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted

<h3 id="write-slice-debug"><code>WriteSliceDebug&lt;T&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteSliceDebug<T: Debug>(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    items: T[..],
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes a borrowed run of elements as `[first, second, third]`.
An empty run is `[]`, which is visible where writing nothing would not be. Elements are separated by a comma and
a space, and every element is shown, since a diagnostic that elided part of what it was given would be worse
than a long one.
The run is borrowed and each element is shown through a borrow of it, so a slice of a move-only element type is
shown without disturbing a single one of them.
`spec` is handed to each element unchanged and means whatever that element type makes of it. The brackets and
commas are punctuation and are never padded.
Reports whatever the writer or an element's implementation reported, stopping at the first refusal rather than
continuing through the rest of the run.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Structure.rux#L92)

**Type parameters**

| Name       | Description                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `T: Debug` | the element type, which must know how to show itself |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                                        |
| -------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                                    |
| `items`  | `T[..]`           | the run of elements to show, borrowed for the call |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what to show each element under                    |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted
